title: 5 Simple Steps for Solving Any Recursive Problem
beats: Recursion feels harder than most CS topics; promise five steps and three problems of rising difficulty
Problem 1: sum 0..n; pose it, hint that iterative/closed forms exist but ask for recursive
Step 1: simplest input (n=0 gives 0) becomes the base case
Step 2: try examples; visualize sum as a triangle of blocks
Step 3: pause and ask viewer to spot how n=5 relates to n=4; answer is add 5
Step 4 generalize to k; step 5 code almost writes itself from base case plus pattern
Trace sum(5) unravelling down to base then building back up
Recursive leap of faith: assume smaller case works; admits viewer may be hesitant
Problem 2: grid paths, down/right only; show 2x4 gives 4 and 3x3 gives 6 before solving
Base case: any dimension 1 gives one path; flags base cases may be revised later
Generate a sweep of neighbouring examples on purpose so relations are visible
Narrow to three examples; one-to-one path correspondence (add a down step or a right step)
Asks 'is that coincidence?'; tests 3x4 case by constructing from 3x3 and 2x4
Problem 3: count partitions of n with parts up to m; two examples (6,4 gives 9; 5,5 gives 7)
Admits it looks intimidating; base cases n=0 gives 1 (empty partition), m=0 gives 0
Many close examples again; invites pause
Notice smaller-m partitions reappear inside larger ones ('crazy sorcery'), verified on (7,4)
Split into partitions without m (subset) and with m (subtract m, one-to-one correspondence)
Generalize recurrence; fix negative-n corner case, revising base cases after the pattern; six lines of code
Recap five steps and what you did, close with practice advice

new_moves.name: predict-then-verify-on-larger
new_moves.what: After spotting a pattern on small cases, test it on a bigger unseen case built by the pattern, asking if it is a coincidence

new_moves.name: examples-sweep-by-design
new_moves.what: Choose examples adjacent to each other on purpose and tell the viewer why

new_moves.name: revisit-base-after-pattern
new_moves.what: Explicitly say base cases may need edits after the recurrence, then show it

new_moves.name: narrow-focus-hint
new_moves.what: When the viewer may be lost, zoom to the three relevant examples as a hint

theory: The video teaches a procedure, not an answer: a fixed five-step ritual is run three times on harder problems so the viewer rehearses the habit. Insight is delegated to the viewer through pauses, then confirmed with a bijection argument and a bigger verify case. The distinctive move is guiding attention (neighbouring examples, three-example hint) rather than explaining the pattern.
velocity: Make 'playbook' a visible numbered checklist that the scene builder reuses across problems so learners internalize the ritual
Scene builder: generate sweeps of adjacent examples, then highlight the 3 relevant ones when the learner stalls (ghost-hands hint)
Orchestrator: insert a pause-and-predict beat before revealing the relation; voice waits for a learner guess
Add a verify-on-new-case beat after every discovered rule, with a bigger input the learner has not seen
Learner model: hold off on code/notation until relation is stated in words; evals check notation arrives after the concept
